meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen's essay got a zero and nobody called me first.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Go on.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Owen wrote it over the weekend, so he pasted it in from wherever he'd saved it. Can I open that history myself?
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. Then tell me whether anyone asked Owen about this before the zero went in.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time. Pull up the play and search it in front of me.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Okay, I'll read both. But people change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale. That's what drafting is.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him before the zero. But a seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck" and you call that proof? I'll want that note in an email.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
A forty-minute in-class piece and a take-home essay are different things. So what are you asking for, Hale?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to use it alone. Now answer the question I asked: what do you want done?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4. A private rewrite, not in front of his class, and your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his file. I'll agree to it to put this behind him, not because of anything he did.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Okay. In writing tonight, and the principal gets a copy. Everything else I'll put in my email.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, after school, not during a class. Put the day and the time in the email tonight.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. And Thursday, after school. Is there anything else you need to say?
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The note from November 2 and those version history entries, attached to the email tonight. Then I'm done.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, with the new mark replacing the zero, nothing placed on Owen's record, and your confirmation of all of it in writing. I still require the day and time of the rewrite, your November 2 note, and the version history entries you showed me, attached. I expect it all in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Her last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, the new mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, and the principal copied, and she still wants your November 2 note, the version history entries and the day and time in writing tonight. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You offered 4.4 only after laying out your dated documents one at a time and letting her check each herself, so by then the rewrite answered her demand about his record and she had grounds to accept it.
What cost ground: Your November 2 conversation with Owen rested on your own note, which she could not check, so she demanded it on paper instead of treating it as settled.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence came close when you said the document was created at 11:31 PM on October 28 and the text arrived in two large edits, and she answered by writing the times down and pushing on procedure; that proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said Owen had written it over the weekend and pasted it in, you told her only that she could check the history, so answer that point directly before moving to your next document.
